title.zh: 卷三 補帝紀第三 文襄帝
title.raw: 卷三 補帝紀第三 文襄帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wenxiang

sentences.zh: 世宗文襄皇帝，諱澄，字子惠，神武長子也，母曰婁太后。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong Wenxiang, taboo name Cheng, style Zihui, was the eldest son of Shenwu; his mother was Empress Dowager Lou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong of Northern Qi, bore the personal name Cheng and the style Zihui. He was the eldest son of Gao Huan; his mother was Empress Dowager Lou.

sentences.zh: 生而岐嶷，神武異之。

translations.literal: From birth he was precocious and sharp; Shenwu regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was precocious and keen; Gao Huan took him for a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 魏中興元年，立為渤海王世子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing of Wei he was established as heir of the Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongxing 1 (531) he was made heir to the Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 就杜詢講學，敏悟過人，詢甚嘆服。

translations.literal: He went to Du Xun to study; his quick comprehension surpassed others, and Xun greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Du Xun; his quickness of mind surpassed all others, and Du Xun came to admire him deeply.

sentences.zh: 二年，加侍中、開府儀同三司，尚孝靜帝妹馮翊長公主，時年十二，神情儁爽，便若成人。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given Palace Attendant, Grand Lord Equal to Three Imperator, and married the Princess Chang of Fengyi, sister of Emperor Xiaojing; he was then twelve, with a handsome and spirited bearing, already like a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Lord Equal to Three Imperator and married Princess Chang of Fengyi, Emperor Xiaojing's sister. He was twelve, handsome and spirited, already bearing himself like a man.

sentences.zh: 神武試問以時事得失，辨析無不中理，自是軍國籌策皆預之。

translations.literal: Shenwu tested him on the gains and losses of current affairs; his analysis never missed the mark, and from then on he took part in every military and state plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan tested him on the affairs of the day; his analysis never missed the mark, and from then on he was included in every plan of war and state.

sentences.zh: 天平元年，加使持節、尚書令、大行臺、幷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping he was given Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping 1 (534) he received Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and the inspectorship of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 三年，入輔朝政，加領左右、京畿大都督。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered to assist court governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered the capital to assist in governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and made Grand Commander of the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 時人雖聞器識，猶以少年期之，而機略嚴明，事無凝滯，於是朝野振肅。

translations.literal: Though people had heard of his talent and judgment, they still looked on him as a youth; yet his strategy was strict and clear, affairs never stalled, and court and countryside were stirred to solemn order.
translations.idiomatic: Though men had heard of his talent, they still treated him as a youth; yet his plans were strict and clear, nothing hung fire, and court and countryside alike were stirred to order.

sentences.zh: 元象元年，攝吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he acted as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang 1 (538) he served as acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 魏自崔亮以後。

translations.literal: In Wei, since Cui Liang's time.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Wei, since the time of Cui Liang,

sentences.zh: 選人常以年勞為制，文襄乃釐改前式，銓擢唯在得人。

translations.literal: appointments had been governed by years of service; Wenxiang then reformed the former practice, and selection and promotion rested only on getting the right men.
translations.idiomatic: appointments had been governed by seniority; Gao Cheng reformed the old practice so that selection rested only on finding the right men.

sentences.zh: 又沙汰尚書郎，妙選人地以充之。

translations.literal: He also sifted the clerks of the Masters of Writing and finely chose men of talent and standing to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: He also sifted the clerks of the Masters of Writing and chose men of talent and standing to fill the posts.

sentences.zh: 至于才名之士，咸被薦擢，假有未居顯位者，皆致之門下，以為賓客，每山園游燕，必見招攜，執射賦詩，各盡其所長，以為娛適。

translations.literal: As for men of talent and name, all were recommended and promoted; even those not yet in high office he brought into his household as retainers. Whenever he toured gardens and hills he always summoned them; they shot arrows, composed verse, and each displayed his strength — all for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent and reputation he recommended and promoted; those not yet in high office he took into his household as retainers. Whenever he toured gardens and hills he summoned them; they shot arrows, composed verse, and each showed his gift — all for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，加大將軍，領中書監，仍攝吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was given Grand General, Director of the Secretariat Supervisor, and still acted as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe 2 (540) he was made Grand General and Director of the Secretariat Supervisor while still serving as acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 自正光已後，天下多事，在任羣官，廉潔者寡。

translations.literal: From after Zhenguang the realm had been in turmoil, and among officials in office few were honest.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguang era the realm had been in turmoil, and among officials in office few were honest.

sentences.zh: 文襄乃奏吏部郎崔暹為御史中尉，糾劾權豪，無所縱捨，於是風俗更始，私枉路絕。

translations.literal: Wenxiang then memorialized to make Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful and wealthy without sparing any, and custom was renewed — private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.

sentences.zh: 乃牓於街衢，具論經國政術，仍開直言之路，有論事上書苦言切至者，皆優容之。

translations.literal: He posted notices in the streets setting forth the arts of governing the state, and opened a path for blunt speech; those who submitted memorials or letters with bitter and penetrating words he all received with favor.
translations.idiomatic: He posted notices in the streets setting forth the arts of governing the state and opened a path for blunt speech; those who submitted memorials or letters with bitter and penetrating words he all received with favor.

sentences.zh: 武定四年十一月，神武西討，不豫班師，文襄馳赴軍所，侍衛還晉陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Wuding, Shenwu campaigned west and, falling ill, withdrew the army; Wenxiang raced to the army's camp, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Wuding 4 (546), Gao Huan marched west, fell ill, and withdrew; Gao Cheng raced to the army, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 五年正月丙午，神武崩，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, on bingwu, Shenwu died; the death was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wuding 5 (547), on bingwu day, Gao Huan died; the death was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，司徒侯景據河南反，潁州刺史司馬世雲以城應之。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Minister of Works Hou Jing held Henan in rebellion, and Sima Shiyun, Inspector of Ying Province, opened the city to him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Minister of Works Hou Jing rebelled and held Henan, and Ying Inspector Sima Shiyun opened the city to him.

sentences.zh: 景誘執豫州刺史高元成、襄州刺史李密、廣州刺史暴顯等。

translations.literal: Jing lured and seized Yuzhou Inspector Gao Yuancheng, Xiangzhou Inspector Li Mi, Guangzhou Inspector Bao Xian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing lured and seized Yuzhou Inspector Gao Yuancheng, Xiangzhou Inspector Li Mi, Guangzhou Inspector Bao Xian, and others.

sentences.zh: 遣司空韓軌率衆討之。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬申，文襄朝於鄴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on renshen, Wenxiang attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on renshen day, Gao Cheng attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，韓軌等自潁州班師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi, Han Gui and the others withdrew the army from Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi day, Han Gui and the others withdrew from Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，文襄還晉陽，乃發喪，告喻文武，陳神武遺志。

translations.literal: On dingchou Wenxiang returned to Jinyang, then announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Shenwu's final wishes.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang, announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Gao Huan's final wishes.

sentences.zh: 七月戊戌，魏帝詔以文襄為使持節、大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行臺、渤海王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu, the Wei Emperor edicted that Wenxiang be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the Eastern Wei emperor edicted that Gao Cheng be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 文襄啟辭位，願停王爵。

translations.literal: Wenxiang memorialized to decline the post and wished to relinquish the princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng memorialized to decline and wished to relinquish the princely rank.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏帝詔太原公洋攝理軍國，遣中使敦喻。

translations.literal: On renyin the Wei Emperor edicted that Duke of Taiyuan Yang administer military and state affairs, and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day the emperor edicted that Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang administer military and state affairs and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.

sentences.zh: 八月戊辰，文襄啟申神武遺令，請減國邑分封將督，各有差。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuchen, Wenxiang memorialized to carry out Shenwu's final command, asking to reduce the fiefs of the realm and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuchen day, Gao Cheng memorialized to carry out Gao Huan's final command, asking to reduce the royal fief and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.

sentences.zh: 辛未，朝鄴，固辭丞相。

translations.literal: On xinwei he attended court at Ye and firmly declined the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day he attended court at Ye and firmly declined the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 魏帝詔曰：「旣朝野攸憑，安危所系，不得令遂本懷，須有權奪，可復前大將軍，餘如故。」

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor edicted: "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your original wish; there must be a taking of authority by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor edicted, "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your wish; authority must be taken by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."

sentences.zh: 議者咸云侯景猶有北望之心，但信命不至耳。

translations.literal: Discussants all said Hou Jing still had a mind to look north, but only the command had not reached him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who debated the matter all said Hou Jing still looked northward, but only the command had not reached him.

sentences.zh: 又景將蔡遵道北歸，稱景有悔過之心。

translations.literal: Again Jing's officer Cai Zundao returned north and said Jing had a mind to repent.
translations.idiomatic: Again Hou Jing's officer Cai Zundao returned north and said Hou Jing wished to repent.

sentences.zh: 王以為信然，謂可誘而致，乃遺景書曰：

translations.literal: The Prince believed it true and thought he could be lured back; he sent Jing a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng believed it and thought he could be lured back; he sent Hou Jing a letter saying,

sentences.zh: 先王與司徒契闊夷險，孤子相依，偏所眷屬，義貫終始，情存歲寒。

translations.literal: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you — you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.
translations.idiomatic: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you—you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.

sentences.zh: 待為國士者乃立漆身之節，饋以一餐者便致扶輪之效，況其重於此乎？

translations.literal: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel — how much more when the bond was weightier than this?
translations.idiomatic: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel—how much more when the bond was weightier than this?

sentences.zh: 常以故舊之義，欲將子孫相托，方為秦晉之匹，共成劉、范之親。

translations.literal: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.

sentences.zh: 況聞負杖行歌，便以狼顧反噬，不蹈忠臣之路，便陷叛人之地。

translations.literal: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.

sentences.zh: 力不足以自強，勢不足以自保，率烏合之衆，為累卵之危。

translations.literal: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.

sentences.zh: 西取救於宇文，南請援於蕭氏，以狐疑之心，為首鼠之事。

translations.literal: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house — with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.
translations.idiomatic: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house—with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.

sentences.zh: 入秦則秦人不容，歸吳則吳人不信。

translations.literal: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.
translations.idiomatic: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.

sentences.zh: 當是不逞之人，曲為無端之說，遂懷市虎之疑，乃致投杼之惑。

translations.literal: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.
translations.idiomatic: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.

sentences.zh: 比來舉止，事已可見，人相疑誤，想自覺知。

translations.literal: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.

sentences.zh: 闔門大小，悉在司寇，意謂李氏未滅，猶言少卿可反。

translations.literal: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.
translations.idiomatic: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.

sentences.zh: 孤子無狀招禍，丁天酷罰，但禮由權奪，志在忘私，聊遣偏裨，前驅致討，南兗、揚州，應時剋復。

translations.literal: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment — yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.
translations.idiomatic: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment—yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 即欲乘機，席捲縣瓠，屬以炎暑，欲為後圖，且令還師，待時更舉。

translations.literal: I meant to seize the moment, sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to seize the moment and sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.

sentences.zh: 今寒膠向折，白露將團，方憑國靈，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 器械精新，士馬強盛，內外感恩，上下戮力，三令五申，可赴湯火。

translations.literal: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.

sentences.zh: 使旗鼓相望，埃塵相接，勢如沃雪，事等注熒。

translations.literal: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.
translations.idiomatic: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.

sentences.zh: 夫明者去危就安，智者轉禍為福，甯人負我，不我負人，當開從善之途，使有改迷之路。

translations.literal: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others — open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.
translations.idiomatic: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others—open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.

sentences.zh: 若能卷甲來朝，垂橐還闕者，即當授豫州，必使終君身世。

translations.literal: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.
translations.idiomatic: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.

sentences.zh: 所部文武更不追攝，進得保其祿位，退則不喪功名。

translations.literal: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.
translations.idiomatic: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.

sentences.zh: 今王思政等皆孤軍偏將，遠來深入，然其性命在君掌握，脫能刺之，想有餘力。

translations.literal: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand — if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand—if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.

sentences.zh: 節相加授，永保疆埸。

translations.literal: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 君門眷屬，可以無患，寵妻愛子，亦送相還，仍為通家，共成親好。

translations.literal: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back — we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.
translations.idiomatic: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back—we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.

sentences.zh: 君今不能東封函谷，南面稱孤，受制於人，威名頓盡。

translations.literal: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.

sentences.zh: 得地不欲自守，聚衆不以為強，空使身有背叛之名，家有惡逆之禍，覆宗絕嗣，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong — in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong—in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.

sentences.zh: 戴天履地，能無愧乎！

translations.literal: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot — can you be without shame!
translations.idiomatic: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot—can you be without shame!

sentences.zh: 孤子今日不應遣此，但見蔡遵道云：「司徒本無西歸之心，深有悔過之意」，未知此語為虛為實。

translations.literal: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say: "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent" — I do not know whether these words are empty or real.
translations.idiomatic: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say, "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent"—I do not know whether these words are empty or real.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之理，想自圖之。

translations.literal: The logic of fortune and calamity — I think you will weigh it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The logic of fortune and calamity—I think you will weigh it yourself.

sentences.zh: 景報書曰：

translations.literal: Jing replied in a letter:
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing replied in a letter:

sentences.zh: 僕鄉曲布衣，本乖藝用，出身為國，綿曆二紀，犯危履難，豈避風霜，遂得富貴當年，榮華身世。

translations.literal: I, a humble man of the village lanes, by nature unfit for arts and use, entered service for the state and have passed two decades, braving peril and treading hardship without shunning wind and frost — thus I gained wealth in those years and glory in this life.
translations.idiomatic: I, a humble man of the village lanes, by nature unfit for arts and use, entered service for the state and have passed two decades, braving peril and treading hardship without shunning wind and frost—thus I gained wealth in those years and glory in this life.

sentences.zh: 一旦舉旗掞，援鼓枹，北面相抗者何哉？

translations.literal: Why did I once raise the banner and beat the drum and face north in resistance?
translations.idiomatic: Why did I once raise the banner and beat the drum and face north in resistance?

sentences.zh: 寔以畏懼危亡，恐招禍害故耳。

translations.literal: Truly because I feared peril and death and dreaded drawing calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because I feared peril and death and dreaded drawing calamity.

sentences.zh: 往年之暮，尊王遘疾，神不祐善，祈禱莫瘳。

translations.literal: In the late months of the year before, the honored king fell ill; the spirits did not bless the good, and prayers brought no cure.
translations.idiomatic: In the late months of the year before, the honored king fell ill; the spirits did not bless the good, and prayers brought no cure.

sentences.zh: 遂使嬖幸弄權，心腹離貳，妻子在宅，無事見圍。

translations.literal: Thus favorites played with power, trusted hearts were divided, and though wife and children were at home they were besieged without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Thus favorites played with power, trusted hearts were divided, and though wife and children were at home they were besieged without cause.

sentences.zh: 及廻歸長社，希自陳狀，簡書未遣，斧鉞已臨。

translations.literal: When I returned to Changshe and hoped to state my case, the summons had not yet been sent and the axe was already at hand.
translations.idiomatic: When I returned to Changshe and hoped to state my case, the summons had not yet been sent and the axe was already at hand.

sentences.zh: 旣旌旗相對，咫尺不遠，飛書每奏，冀申鄙情。

translations.literal: Though banners faced each other and we were not a bowshot apart, I sent letters again and again, hoping to make my humble feeling plain.
translations.idiomatic: Though banners faced each other and we were not a bowshot apart, I sent letters again and again, hoping to make my humble feeling plain.

sentences.zh: 而群帥恃雄，眇然弗顧，連戰推鋒，專欲屠滅。

translations.literal: Yet the commanders relied on their strength and looked down on me; battle followed battle, thrust on thrust, and they sought only to slaughter and destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the commanders relied on their strength and looked down on me; battle followed battle, thrust on thrust, and they sought only to slaughter and destroy.

sentences.zh: 掘圍堰水，僅存三版，舉目相看，命縣漏刻。

translations.literal: They dug ditches and dammed water until only three boards of wall remained; we looked at each other, lives hanging by the dripping clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: They dug ditches and dammed water until only three boards of wall remained; we looked at each other, lives hanging by the dripping clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 不忍死亡，出戰城下，拘秦送地，豈樂為之？

translations.literal: Unable to bear death, I went out to fight below the wall and was seized and sent to Qin — would I do that for pleasure?
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear death, I went out to fight below the wall and was seized and sent to Qin—would I do that for pleasure?

sentences.zh: 禽獸惡死，人倫好生，僕實不辜，桓、莊何罪。

translations.literal: Beasts hate death; human relations love life — I am truly guiltless; what crime had Huan and Zhuang?
translations.idiomatic: Beasts hate death; human relations love life—I am truly guiltless; what crime had Huan and Zhuang?

sentences.zh: 且尊王平昔見與比肩，戮力同心，共獎帝室，雖復權勢參差，寒暑小異，丞相司徒，雁行而已。

translations.literal: Moreover the honored king in former days treated me as an equal; we strove together with one heart and jointly upheld the imperial house — though power was unequal and cold and heat differed slightly, Chancellor and Minister of Works were only like geese in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the honored king in former days treated me as an equal; we strove together with one heart and jointly upheld the imperial house—though power was unequal and cold and heat differed slightly, Chancellor and Minister of Works were only like geese in flight.

sentences.zh: 福祿官榮，自是天爵，勞而後授，理不相干，欲求吞炭，何其謬也！

translations.literal: Fortune, salary, office, and glory are heaven's rank; granted after labor — reason does not connect with seeking to swallow charcoal; how absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune, salary, office, and glory are heaven's rank; granted after labor—reason does not connect with seeking to swallow charcoal; how absurd!

sentences.zh: 然竊人之財，猶謂之盜。

translations.literal: Yet to steal another's goods is still called theft.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to steal another's goods is still called theft.

sentences.zh: 祿去公室，抑謂不取。

translations.literal: Salary taken from the public house — can one say it was not taken?
translations.idiomatic: Salary taken from the public house—can one say it was not taken?

sentences.zh: 今魏德雖衰，天命未改，拜恩私第，何足關言。

translations.literal: Now Wei's virtue though declined, heaven's mandate is not yet changed; to receive favor in a private residence — what need to speak of it?
translations.idiomatic: Now Wei's virtue though declined, heaven's mandate is not yet changed; to receive favor in a private residence—what need to speak of it?

sentences.zh: 賜嗤不能東封函谷，受制於人，當似教僕賢祭仲而褒季氏。

translations.literal: You mock me for being unable to seal Hangu Pass in the east and for being controlled by others — it is as if you praised Jizhong and commended the Ji clan.
translations.idiomatic: You mock me for being unable to seal Hangu Pass in the east and for being controlled by others—it is as if you praised Jizhong and commended the Ji clan.

sentences.zh: 無主之國，在禮未聞，動而不法，將何以訓？

translations.literal: A realm without a lord — in ritual I have not heard of it; to act without law — with what will you instruct?
translations.idiomatic: A realm without a lord—in ritual I have not heard of it; to act without law—with what will you instruct?

sentences.zh: 竊以分財養幼，事歸令終，舍宅存孤，誰雲隙末？

translations.literal: I hold that dividing wealth to nurture the young is a matter of proper ending; leaving a house to preserve the orphan — who would call that a petty grudge?
translations.idiomatic: I hold that dividing wealth to nurture the young is a matter of proper ending; leaving a house to preserve the orphan—who would call that a petty grudge?

sentences.zh: 復言僕衆不足以自強，身危如累卵。

translations.literal: Again you say my host is not enough to strengthen myself and my person is in peril like a pile of eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Again you say my host is not enough to strengthen myself and my person is in peril like a pile of eggs.

sentences.zh: 然億兆夷人，卒降十亂，紂之百克，終自無後，潁川之戰，即是殷監。

translations.literal: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, the ten rebels of Zhou fell; Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs — the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, the ten rebels of Zhou fell; Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs—the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.

sentences.zh: 輕重由人，非鼎在德，苟能忠信，雖弱必強，殷憂啟聖，處危何苦。

translations.literal: Weight and light depend on the man, not the tripod on virtue; if one can be loyal and faithful, though weak one must become strong; deep sorrow opens the sage, and dwelling in peril — what hardship is there?
translations.idiomatic: Weight and light depend on the man, not the tripod on virtue; if one can be loyal and faithful, though weak one must become strong; deep sorrow opens the sage, and dwelling in peril—what hardship is there?

sentences.zh: 況今梁道邕熙，招攜以禮，被我虎文，縻之好爵，方欲苑五岳而池四海，掃氛穢以拯黎元。

translations.literal: Moreover now Liang's way is harmonious and bright; it gathers men by ritual, covers them with tiger-pattern robes, and ties them with noble ranks — it intends to park the five peaks as a garden and pool the four seas, sweep foul vapors and save the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover now Liang's way is harmonious and bright; it gathers men by ritual, covers them with tiger-pattern robes, and ties them with noble ranks—it intends to park the five peaks as a garden and pool the four seas, sweep foul vapors and save the black-haired people.

sentences.zh: 東羈甌越，西道汧隴，吳越悍勁，帶甲千羣，秦兵冀馬，控弦十萬，大風一振，枯幹必摧，凝霜暫落，秋帶自殞，此而為弱，誰足稱雄？

translations.literal: East it bridles Ou and Yue; west it opens the road to Qian and Long; Wu and Yue are fierce and strong, girded with armor in thousands; Qin troops and Ji horses, bows drawn in tens of thousands — one blast of great wind and dry trunks must break; frost gathers for a moment and autumn girdles fall of themselves — if this is called weak, who is fit to be called strong?
translations.idiomatic: East it bridles Ou and Yue; west it opens the road to Qian and Long; Wu and Yue are fierce and strong, girded with armor in thousands; Qin troops and Ji horses, bows drawn in tens of thousands—one blast of great wind and dry trunks must break; frost gathers for a moment and autumn girdles fall of themselves—if this is called weak, who is fit to be called strong?

sentences.zh: 又見誣兩端，受疑二國，斟酌物情，一何太甚！

translations.literal: Again I see slander of wavering between two sides and suspicion from two states — weighing human feeling, how excessively!
translations.idiomatic: Again I see slander of wavering between two sides and suspicion from two states—weighing human feeling, how excessively!

sentences.zh: 昔陳平背楚，歸漢則強，百里出虞，入秦斯霸。

translations.literal: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.

sentences.zh: 蓋昏明由主，用舍在人，奉禮而行，神其吐邪！

translations.literal: Dark and bright depend on the lord; use and discard depend on the man — follow ritual in action, and the spirits will reject evil!
translations.idiomatic: Dark and bright depend on the lord; use and discard depend on the man—follow ritual in action, and the spirits will reject evil!

sentences.zh: 書稱士馬精新，剋日齊舉，誇張形勢，必欲相滅。

translations.literal: Your letter speaks of sharp soldiers and horses and fixing a day for joint advance, exaggerating the situation and surely wishing mutual destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter speaks of sharp soldiers and horses and fixing a day for joint advance, exaggerating the situation and surely wishing mutual destruction.

sentences.zh: 切以寒膠白露，節候乃同，秋風揚塵，馬首何異。

translations.literal: Truly cold glue and white dew — the season is the same; wind raises dust and the horses' heads — what difference is there?
translations.idiomatic: Truly cold glue and white dew—the season is the same; wind raises dust and the horses' heads—what difference is there?

sentences.zh: 徒知北方之力爭，未識西南之合從，苟欲狥意於前途，不覺坑穽在其側。

translations.literal: You know only the north's struggle for strength and do not see the southwest's alliance — if you wish to follow your whim on the road ahead, you do not notice the pitfall at your side.
translations.idiomatic: You know only the north's struggle for strength and do not see the southwest's alliance—if you wish to follow your whim on the road ahead, you do not notice the pitfall at your side.

sentences.zh: 去危就安，今歸正朔；

translations.literal: Leave peril for safety — now return to the orthodox calendar;
translations.idiomatic: Leave peril for safety—now return to the orthodox calendar;

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，已脫網羅。

translations.literal: turn calamity into blessing — already escaped the net.
translations.idiomatic: turn calamity into blessing—already escaped the net.

sentences.zh: 彼當嗤僕之過迷，此亦笑君之晦昧。

translations.literal: They will mock my past confusion; this too laughs at your obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: They will mock my past confusion; this too laughs at your obscurity.

sentences.zh: 今引二邦，揚旌北討，熊虎齊奮，克復中原，荊、襄、廣、潁，已屬關右，項城、縣瓠，亦奉江南，幸自取之，何勞見援。

translations.literal: Now I lead two states, raise banners and march north to attack; bears and tigers strive together, recover the central plains — Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the Guanxi; Xiangcheng and Xianhu already submit to the Jiangnan — take them yourself; what need to ask aid?
translations.idiomatic: Now I lead two states, raise banners and march north to attack; bears and tigers strive together, recover the central plains—Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the Guanxi; Xiangcheng and Xianhu already submit to the Jiangnan—take them yourself; what need to ask aid?

sentences.zh: 然權變非一，理有萬途，為君計者，莫若割地兩和，三分鼎峙，燕、衛、趙、晉，足相俸祿，齊、曹、宋、魯，悉歸大樑。

translations.literal: Yet expedients are not one; reason has ten thousand paths. For your plan, nothing surpasses ceding land and making peace in two parts, three shares standing like the tripod — Yan, Wei, Zhao, and Jin enough for salary; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all return to Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet expedients are not one; reason has ten thousand paths. For your plan, nothing surpasses ceding land and making peace in two parts, three shares standing like the tripod—Yan, Wei, Zhao, and Jin enough for salary; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all return to Great Liang.

sentences.zh: 使僕得輸力南朝，北敦姻好，束帛自行，戎車不駕，僕立當世之功，君卒父禰之業，各保疆壘，聽享歲時，百姓乂寧，四人安堵。

translations.literal: Let me lend strength to the southern court, north I honor kinship by marriage; silks go of themselves, war chariots need not be driven — I stand and achieve merit for the age, you finish your fathers' and grandfathers' enterprise; each keeps his frontier, each enjoys the seasons; the hundred surnames are at peace, the four classes dwell secure.
translations.idiomatic: Let me lend strength to the southern court, north I honor kinship by marriage; silks go of themselves, war chariots need not be driven—I stand and achieve merit for the age, you finish your fathers' and grandfathers' enterprise; each keeps his frontier, each enjoys the seasons; the hundred surnames are at peace, the four classes dwell secure.

sentences.zh: 孰若驅農夫於壟畝，抗勁敵於三方，避干戈於首尾，當鋒鏑於心腹。

translations.literal: How does that compare with driving farmers from the fields, facing fierce enemies on three sides, avoiding weapons at head and tail, and meeting blades and arrows at the heart?
translations.idiomatic: How does that compare with driving farmers from the fields, facing fierce enemies on three sides, avoiding weapons at head and tail, and meeting blades and arrows at the heart?

sentences.zh: 縱太公為將，不能獲存，歸之高明，何以克濟。

translations.literal: Even if the Grand Duke were general, he could not survive; return to the high and bright — how could success be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Grand Duke were general, he could not survive; return to the high and bright—how could success be achieved?

sentences.zh: 來書曰，妻子老幼悉在司寇，以此見要，庶其可反。

translations.literal: Your letter says that wife, children, and elders are all in the Ministry of Justice, and you use this to coerce me, hoping I might return.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter says my wife, children, and elders are all held by the Ministry of Justice, and that you mean to use them to force my return.

sentences.zh: 當是見疑褊心，未識大趣。

translations.literal: Surely this shows a suspicious and narrow mind, not understanding the larger design.
translations.idiomatic: This can only be the work of a suspicious and petty mind that does not grasp the larger design.

sentences.zh: 昔王陵附漢，母在不歸；

translations.literal: Long ago Wang Ling sided with Han while his mother lived and did not return;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Wang Ling sided with Han while his mother was alive in Chu and would not return;

sentences.zh: 太上囚楚，乞羹自若。

translations.literal: the Dowager Empress was imprisoned in Chu yet begged for soup as calmly as ever.
translations.idiomatic: the Dowager Empress was held prisoner in Chu yet asked for soup as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 矧伊妻子，而可介意。

translations.literal: How much less should one fuss over wife and children!
translations.idiomatic: How much less, then, should one make a fuss over wife and children!

sentences.zh: 脫謂誅之有益，欲止不能，殺之無損，復加阬戮，家累在君，何關僕也。

translations.literal: If you say killing them would help, you cannot stop wanting to; killing them would do you no good, yet you would still slaughter them. Your hostages are in your hands—what concern are they of mine?
translations.idiomatic: If you think killing them would serve some purpose, you cannot restrain yourself; if it would do you no good, you would still butcher them anyway. Your hostages are in your hands—what is that to me?

sentences.zh: 遵道所說，頗亦非虛，故重陳辭，更論款曲。

translations.literal: What Zundao said was not entirely empty, so I restate my case and speak again of heartfelt matters.
translations.idiomatic: What Zundao reported was not wholly empty, and so I restate my case and speak again in earnest.

sentences.zh: 昔與盟主，事等琴瑟，讒人間之，翻為讐敵。

translations.literal: Once I and the alliance leader were harmonious as lute and zither; slanderers set us apart, and we became enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Once the alliance leader and I were as harmonious as lute and zither; slanderers came between us, and we became enemies.

sentences.zh: 撫弦搦矢，不覺傷懷，裂帛還書，其何能述。

translations.literal: Touching the strings, grasping the arrow—I cannot but feel grief; torn silk returned in reply—how can words express it?
translations.idiomatic: To touch the strings or grasp the arrow is to feel grief anew; to tear silk and send it back in reply—how can words say enough?

sentences.zh: 王尋覽書，問誰為作。

translations.literal: When the Prince had read the letter, he asked who had written it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng had read the letter, he asked who had written it.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「其行臺郎王偉。

translations.literal: Someone said: "It was his Mobile Court Gentleman Wang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "It was his mobile-court gentleman Wang Wei.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「偉才如此，何因不使我知？

translations.literal: " The Prince said: "With talent like this, why was I not told?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "With talent like this, why was I not told?

sentences.zh: 」王欲間景於梁，又與景書而謬其辭，云本使景陽叛，欲與圖西，西人知之，故景更與圖南為事。

translations.literal: " The Prince wished to drive a wedge between Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally had Jing stir rebellion at Jingyang and planned with him to strike west; when Western Wei learned this, Jing turned instead to scheming with the south.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng wished to drive a wedge between Hou Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally sent Jing to stir rebellion at Jingyang and meant to plot the west together; when Western Wei learned of it, Jing turned instead to plotting with the south.

sentences.zh: 漏其書於梁，梁人亦不之信。

translations.literal: He leaked the letter to Liang, but the Liang people also did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: He leaked the letter to Liang, but the Liang court did not believe it either.

sentences.zh: 壬申，東魏主與王獵於鄴東，馳逐如飛。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with the Prince east of Ye, racing as if flying.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with Gao Cheng east of Ye, galloping as if in flight.

sentences.zh: 監衛都督烏那羅受工伐從後呼曰：「天子莫走馬，大將軍怒。

translations.literal: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind: "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind, "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!

sentences.zh: 」王嘗侍飲，舉大觴曰：「臣澄勸陛下酒。

translations.literal: " Once, while attending him at drink, the Prince raised a great goblet and said: "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending him at drink, Gao Cheng raised a great goblet and said, "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink.

sentences.zh: 」東魏主不悅曰：「自古無不亡之國，朕亦何用如此生！

translations.literal: " The Eastern Wei emperor said displeased: "Since antiquity no state has failed to perish—why should I cling so to life!
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor said, displeased, "Since antiquity no state has failed to perish—why should I cling so to life!

sentences.zh: 」王怒曰：「朕！

translations.literal: " The Prince raged: "Imperial We!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng raged, "Imperial We!

sentences.zh: 朕！

translations.literal: Imperial We!
translations.idiomatic: Imperial We!

sentences.zh: 狗腳朕！

translations.literal: Imperial We with dog's feet!
translations.idiomatic: Dog-footed Imperial We!

sentences.zh: 」使崔季舒毆之三拳，奮衣而出。

translations.literal: " He had Cui Jishu strike him three blows with the fist, then flung his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He had Cui Jishu strike him three blows with the fist, then flung his robes aside and stormed out.

sentences.zh: 尋遣季舒入謝。

translations.literal: Soon he sent Jishu in to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent Jishu in to apologize.

sentences.zh: 東魏主賜季舒彩，季舒未敢即受，啟之於王，王使取一段。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to the Prince, who told him to take one bolt.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to Gao Cheng, who told him to take one bolt.

sentences.zh: 東魏主以四百疋與之，曰：「亦一段耳。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei emperor gave him four hundred bolts and said: "That too is only one bolt.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor gave him four hundred bolts and said, "That too is only one bolt.

sentences.zh: 」東魏主不堪憂辱，詠謝靈運詩曰：「韓亡子房奮，秦帝魯連恥。

translations.literal: " Unable to bear the anguish and humiliation, the Eastern Wei emperor recited a poem of Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zhang Liang rose in zeal; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhong felt shame.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the anguish and humiliation, the Eastern Wei emperor recited a poem of Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zhang Liang rose in zeal; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhong felt shame.

sentences.zh: 本自江海人，忠義感君子。

translations.literal: Born from river and sea, loyalty and righteousness move the noble heart.
translations.idiomatic: Born from river and sea, loyalty and righteousness move the noble heart.

sentences.zh: 」因流涕。

translations.literal: " And he wept.
translations.idiomatic: And he wept.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，王南臨黎陽，濟於虎牢，自洛陽從太行而反晉陽。

translations.literal: On xinhai of the third month, the Prince went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang by way of Taihang from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai of the third month Gao Cheng went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang from Luoyang by way of the Taihang.

sentences.zh: 於路遺書百僚，以相戒勵。

translations.literal: On the road he left letters to the hundred officials as mutual admonition and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he left letters to the hundred officials, admonishing and encouraging them.

sentences.zh: 朝野承風，莫不震肅。

translations.literal: Court and countryside caught the wind of it; none failed to be shaken into awe.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside caught the wind of it; none failed to be shaken into awe.

sentences.zh: 又令朝臣牧宰各舉賢良及驍武膽略堪守邊城，務得其才，不拘職業。

translations.literal: He also ordered court ministers and district governors each to recommend the worthy and brave with the boldness and strategy to hold border towns, seeking only talent regardless of occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered court ministers and district governors each to recommend the worthy and the brave with the boldness and strategy to hold border towns, seeking talent alone and not binding themselves to rank or trade.

sentences.zh: 六月，王巡北邊城戍，賑賜有差。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Prince toured northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Gao Cheng toured the northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 七月，王還晉陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Prince returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，王遇盜而殂，時年二十九。

translations.literal: On xinmao the Prince fell to assassins and died; he was twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Gao Cheng fell to assassins and died; he was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 葬于峻成陵。

translations.literal: He was buried at Juncheng Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Juncheng Tomb.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，追諡為文襄皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenxiang, with the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 時有童謠曰：「百尺高竿摧折，水底燃燈燈滅。

translations.literal: At the time a children's song ran: "A hundred-foot pole snaps; lamps lit beneath the water go out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a children's song ran, "A hundred-foot pole snaps; lamps lit beneath the water go out.

sentences.zh: 」識者以為王將殂之兆也。

translations.literal: " Those who understood took it as an omen that the Prince would die.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood took it as an omen that Gao Cheng would die.

sentences.zh: 數日前，崔季舒無故於北宮門外諸貴之前誦鮑明遠詩曰：「將軍旣下世，部曲亦罕存。

translations.literal: Days before, Cui Jishu for no apparent reason before the nobles outside the North Palace Gate recited a poem of Bao Mingyuan: "The general having left this world, his followers scarcely remain.
translations.idiomatic: Days before, Cui Jishu for no apparent reason recited before the nobles outside the North Palace Gate a poem of Bao Mingyuan: "The general having left this world, his followers scarcely remain.

sentences.zh: 」聲甚淒斷，淚不能已，見者莫不怪之。

translations.literal: " His voice was deeply mournful and tears would not stop; all who saw it found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: His voice was deeply mournful and tears would not stop; all who saw it found it strange.

sentences.zh: 初，梁將蘭欽子京為東魏所虜，王命以配廚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of Liang General Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; the Prince ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of the Liang general Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; Gao Cheng ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.

sentences.zh: 欽請贖之，王不許。

translations.literal: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; the Prince refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; Gao Cheng refused.

sentences.zh: 京再訴，王使監廚蒼頭薛豐洛杖之，曰：「更訴當殺爾。

translations.literal: Jing appealed again; the Prince had kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said: "Complain again and you will be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing appealed again; Gao Cheng had the kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said, "Complain again and you will be killed.

sentences.zh: 」京與其黨六人謀作亂。

translations.literal: " Jing and six of his cohort plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and six of his cohort plotted mutiny.

sentences.zh: 時王居北城東柏堂蒞政，以寵琅邪公主，欲其來往無所避忌，所有侍衛，皆出於外。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gao Cheng held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.

sentences.zh: 太史啟言宰輔星甚微，變不出一月。

translations.literal: The court astronomer reported that the minister-and-councilor star was very faint; change would come within a month.
translations.idiomatic: The court astronomer reported that the minister-and-councilor star was very faint and that change would come within a month.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「小人新杖之，故嚇我耳。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me.

sentences.zh: 」將欲受禪，與陳元康、崔季舒等屏斥左右，署擬百官。

translations.literal: " About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: About to receive the abdication, he with Chen Yuankang, Cui Jishu, and others dismissed attendants and drafted appointments for the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 京將進食，王却，謂諸人曰：「昨夜夢此奴斫我，宜殺却。

translations.literal: When Jing was about to bring food, the Prince held back and told the others: "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was about to bring food, Gao Cheng held back and told the others, "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him.

sentences.zh: 」京聞之，置刀於盤，冒言進食。

translations.literal: " Jing heard this, hid a knife in the serving tray, and came forward as if to bring food.
translations.idiomatic: Jing heard this, hid a knife in the serving tray, and came forward as if to bring food.

sentences.zh: 王怒曰：「我未索食，爾何據來！

translations.literal: The Prince raged: "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng raged, "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!

sentences.zh: 」京揮刀曰：「來將殺汝！

translations.literal: " Jing swung the knife and said: "I have come to kill you!
translations.idiomatic: Jing swung the knife and said, "I have come to kill you!

sentences.zh: 」王自投傷足，入于床下。

translations.literal: " The Prince threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.

sentences.zh: 賊黨去床，因而見殺。

translations.literal: The assassins dragged him from the bed and so he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The assassins dragged him from the bed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 先是訛言曰：「軟脫帽，床底喘」，其言應矣。

translations.literal: Before this a rumor ran: "Soft hat off, gasping under the bed"—and the words came true.
translations.idiomatic: Before this a rumor ran, "Soft hat off, gasping under the bed"—and the words came true.

sentences.zh: 時太原公洋在城東雙堂，入而討賊，臠割京等，皆漆其頭。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪，徐出言曰：「奴反，大將軍被傷，無大苦也。」

translations.literal: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced: "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."
translations.idiomatic: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced, "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
